correctness.rationale: Every palindrome of a five-run binary word has 0, 2, or 4 transitions. The proof lists every possible factor for each case, including overlap when b=d, and algebraically counts them to obtain the precise defect. The sharp spectrum follows from n>=2D+6 for D>0 and witnesses at each k. Independent center-expansion enumeration for 7776 positive-run tuples and length-spectrum enumeration for n=5..30 matched the formulas; finite checks support rather than prove the universal quantification.

value.rationale: The first non-rich binary words by positive run count occur at exactly five runs, giving this family a canonical boundary role. The theorem identifies a complete exact defect invariant for all positive run compositions, not merely a Boolean richness criterion, and the sharp complete lengthwise range proves which defect sizes can actually occur. Its natural significance is a quantitative structural benchmark for finite-word palindromic deficit and larger-run classifications; it does not rely on an invented downstream theorem.
